newsitem.title: HONG KONG: FOCUS - HK's Hang Seng high rests on HSBC, HK Telecom.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - HK's Hang Seng high rests on HSBC, HK Telecom.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks will need continued investor interest in the big blue chips, in particular Hong Kong Telecom, to maintain the record high levels set in Friday trading, brokers said.
"If we see Hongkong Telecom attracting strong buying, that could support the index above 14,000," said Sam Lok, dealing director at Core Pacific. "If not, we could see a short-term correction."
The Hang Seng Index ended on Friday 190.50 points, or 1.39 percent, higher at a record close of 13,930.80.
The index also set an all time high of 14,047.20, eclipsing the previous high of 14,004.93, set on January 16 of this year.

The Hang Seng, which gained 849.10 points, or 6.49 percent over the week, was thrust to record highs with a shift in investor focus back to solid blue chips and away from the exciting new red chip sector, brokers said.
Turnover, which had been heavy throughout the week, also hit a record of HK$17.85 billion.

"The record highs on Wall Street have given us the room to move ahead today," said Francis Wong, executive director at DBS Securities. "But the bulk of the short-term movement is due to derivative and hedge fund players."
Traders focused on HSBC Holdings from the open on Friday, then included Hongkong Telecom and CITIC Pacific in the basket in the afternoon.
HSBC Holdings hit a record high of HK$219.00 in early afternoon before easing to close at HK$217.00, a gain of HK$7.00 on very heavy turnover of HK$1.58 billion.
The rise in HSBC was fuelled partly by short overing, a continuation of the scramble for the bank's shares seen in London overnight.
The UK's FTSE 100 index leapt to its fifth consecutive record close on Thursday, with HSBC surging to a record on a technical short squeeze, dealers said.
The scramble for Hong Kong Telecom and CITIC Pacific shares in the afternoon added the necessary thrust to push the index to its new highs, Lok said.
The two shares, which had been suspended in the morning, both rose to 1997 record levels before easing slightly in late trade.

CITIC Pacific's announcement that it would sell its 7.75 percent stake in HongKong Telecom to Beijing-based China Everbright was viewed as positive for CITIC, but the market's perception of the impact on Telecom was mixed.

CITIC Pacific rose to HK$45.40, then eased to close HK$0.90 higher at HK$44.40 on trade of HK$612.20 million and Hongkong Telecom shot to HK$15.90, before slipping into negative territory to close down HK$0.50 at HK$14.50 on turnover of HK$776.55 million.
'Chinese liquidity' was the other factor, boosting the index this week, said Wong.
These multi-national hot funds were attracted into the market first into the red chip sector, then rotated to the blue chips and the CITIC-Hongkong Telecom deal, Wong said.
"Volume is very important," said Lok. "Turnover will need to rise to HK$20 billion to push the index higher."
